newsitem.title: UK: Nine airlines form pact to counter BA-American.
newsitem.headline: Nine airlines form pact to counter BA-American.

text.p: Nine major airlines are forming a powerful new global alliance to counter the threat posed by the proposed linkup between British Airways and American Airlines, airline officials told Reuters.
The club is being formed by "like-minded companies of similar quality and with a common vision", Zachary Clark, Air Canada's general manager, passenger sales in Europe, said.
Headed by United Airlines Inc and Deustche Lufthansa AG the new grouping will include airlines from North America, Europe, Asia and Latin America.
It is part of a huge realignment to achieve better economies of scale and higher yields through closer coordination, he added.
Frequent flyer programmes will be merged so as to permit passengers to travel and earn miles on the worldwide network of all nine airlines, Clark said.

Industry sources said the alliance to be launched in mid-May will account for 13 percent of revenue passenger kilometres flown by scheduled airlines and that it will be officially launched as an integral airline product with its own brand name in May.

In addition to Lufthansa and United, it will include Air Canada, Scandinavian Airlines, Thai International and Brazil's Varig. Other airlines like All-Nippon Airways, South African Airways and British Midland are likely join to provide wider global coverage, the sources added.
It aims to steal a five-month March on the BA-American Airlines alliance and to counter the latter's domination of key aviation hubs like London and Dallas.

Before United can participate, however, it must have matching anti-trust immunity from the governments of all partner states to allow the creation of common air fares within the group. So far only United, Lufthansa and SAS can negotiate such common airfares.

Lufthansa's general manager for alliances, Christiane Freuhe, declined to discuss the new venture. "All I can say is that, along with our alliance partners, we are preparing to offer our customers a seamless airline product." The German carrier signed a code-share agreements with United in 1994, with Thai International in 1995 and with SAS and South African in 1996.

The sources said sub-committees covering aircraft procurement, customer relations, computer reservations, frequent flyer programmes, electronic ticketing, airport lounges, safety, inflight services, cargo, personnel management, property, maintenance and network conditions have been working for months on ways to achieve "product commonality" among the nine.
The group's first "universal airport lounge" will be in Bangkok. Similar joint reservations and ticketing offices will be set up around the world.

Clark said he believed the new group could create a single frequent flyer name, membership card and rewards programme in which each airline acts as the issuing agent in the same way banks issue Via or Master Cards.
Like other alliances, he said, it is being driven by a "certain degree of paranoia at the prospect of a BA-American partnership".
A London-based UAL spokesman said: "We think there should be a competitive counter-balance to the BA-American alliance.
"What BA and American are planning is to monopolise London Heathrow and it shouldn't be allowed to happen." -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
